thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Pare Gains After Softer

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Pare Gains After Softer
text:
By Mark economy added 157,000 jobs in July
U.S. major stock-index benchmarks pointed to a flat open on Friday, after the July jobs report came in below expectations, although a drop in the unemployment rate and upward revisions to the previous two months indicated the labor market remained strong.
Investors also grappled with fresh news that China will retaliate with tariffs on $60 billion in U.S. goods, at a time trade deficit rose for the first time in four months.
What are benchmarks doing?
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 16 points, or 0.1%, at 25,289, while those for the S&P 500 index were flat at 2,828. Meanwhile, futures for the tech-laden Nasdaq-100 index added 5 points, or less than 0.1%, to 7,391.
On Thursday, The S&P 500 rose 13.86 points to 2,827.22, for a gain of 0.5%. The Nasdaq Composite Index closed 95.40 points, or 1.2%, higher to 7,802.69, on the back of Apple Inc.'s share (AAPL) advance, but the Dow struggled to hold onto gains, and closed off 7.66 points, or less than 0.1%, to 25,326.16, as that gauge wobbled on trade jitters.
What's driving markets?
Wall Street has been caught up in a battle of concern over the U.S.'s trade spats with China versus optimism over economic and quarterly earnings results that have been outstanding by most measures.
Market reaction to Friday's nonfarm-payrolls report for July was largely muted. The yearly rate of wage gains was unchanged at 2.7%, suggesting no immediate pressure on inflation.
The Federal Reserve's latest policy update affirmed the central bank's plan to raise interest rates at least once more this year, and the jobs report wasn't seen as likely to change that narrative.

What else is on investors' radar?
The trade deficit rose 7% in June trade-deficit-climbs-7-still-on-track-to-hit-10-year-high-2018-08-03)to mark the first increase in four months, keeping the U.S. on track to post the largest annual gap in a decade even as the Trump White House escalates tariffs in an effort to bring it down.
Beyond the jobs report and trade data, investors will await a Markit services report for July is scheduled, with the ISM nonmanufacturing index for the same month due for release at 10 a.m.
Elsewhere, investors are watching signs of economic slowdown in China. A private gauge showed service sector activity in the country continued to grow in July, but at a slower pace than in June (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-caixin-pmi-shows-services-activity-cooling-2018-08-03). China's economy, already facing a slide, has been hurt by the tariff clash with the U.S.
Key Chinese equity index the Shanghai Composite fell 1%, while the Shenzhen Composite declined by 1.7% after hitting a 3 1/2 -year closing low in the prior session.
Which stocks are in focus?
Dish Network Corp. (DISH)soared in premarket trade Friday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dish-networks-stock-soars-as-earnings-and-revenue-beat-expectations-2018-08-03), after the satellite pay-TV service reported better-than-expected second-quarter earnings and revenue.
Shares of CBS Corp. (CBSA) will be in focus after the media company late-Thursday reported second-quarter earnings that came in below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-shares-down-slightly-after-media-company-misses-expectations-2018-08-02) but narrowly topped revenue forecasts for the quarter. CBS on Wednesday said its board of directors had hired outside lawyers to conduct an investigation into allegations that Chief Executive Les Moonves had sexually harassed women. Thursday's earnings statement made no mention (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-earnings-call-oddly-silent-on-allegations-against-moonves-2018-08-02) of Moonves' status.
Apple(AAPL) made history on Thursday become the first U.S. company on Thursday to reach a valuation of $1 trillion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-1-trillion-heres-the-meltdown-that-followed-the-first-company-to-get-there-2018-08-01), following its better-than-expected quarterly results.
